_comment: Tests that are in the wasm32 registry, execute there, and legitimately FAIL there,
because they assert a property of the native host that wasm32 does not have.
They are listed rather than deleted or cfg'd out for two reasons. First, the census:
a test excluded from the registry is invisible, whereas one listed here is executed,
observed to fail, and carries its reason. Second, the gate is bidirectional --
run_wasm_tests.mjs fails the run if a test named here PASSES, so an exclusion that
goes stale (because the platform or the code changed) is reported instead of quietly
suppressing a real test forever. Blanket-suppression is how a green harness ends up
meaning nothing, which is the failure mode this whole exercise exists to rule out.
Native baseline, for contrast: all 94 of these tests pass under

pymath::tests::host_libm_symbols_actuall.reason: Asserts dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, ...) resolves cos/sin/acos/pow in the running process. wasm32 has no dynamic loader at all; pymath::dlsym_ptr is cfg'd to always miss there, because merely declaring the extern emits an env.dlsym import that makes the module non-instantiable in a bare isolate. The property under test is native-only by construction.

pymath::tests::pow_is_not_a_multiply_or_.reason: Asserts that libm pow(x,2.0) differs from x*x for at least one x out of 200000 samples, and pow(c,0.5) from sqrt(c). That divergence is what the B7 pin exists to preserve. On wasm32 pymath::pow falls back to f64::powf, which LLVM folds for constant exponents, so the divergence count is exactly zero and the staleness assertion fires. The test is correct; the platform property it pins is native-only.

dfm::tests::thermal_via_side_round_absor.reason: Same root cause as pymath::tests::pow_is_not_a_multiply_or_a_sqrt -- it asserts the pow-vs-sqrt divergence is non-empty before checking that rounding absorbs it. Zero divergence on wasm32.

dfm::tests::via_annular_area_uses_r_time.reason: Same root cause -- asserts r*r differs from pow(r,2.0) somewhere. Zero divergence on wasm32.
